# ethereum-optimism/Retro-Funding Weekly Report (Apr 26 - 2, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week, development efforts were primarily focused on stabilizing protocol infrastructure and refining the Superchain monitoring stack. Significant attention was directed toward troubleshooting a persistent panic in `op-reth` during version upgrades, which appears linked to parallel trie computation. Additionally, the team clarified key architectural configurations for dispute monitoring and identified potential logic discrepancies in L1 verification for `op-supernode`. Security also remained a priority with the initiation of new automated branch scanning protocols.

## 🛠️ Key Developments
While no new features or refactors were merged during this specific reporting window, the technical focus remained on protocol stability and infrastructure clarification.

### Infrastructure & Monitoring Clarifications
Work this week solidified the operational understanding of the Superchain's monitoring tools. It was confirmed that a single instance of `op-dispute-mon` is capable of concurrently monitoring both CANNON and SUPER_CANNON_KONA game types. Furthermore, the team validated that `op-supernode` is designed to function as a valid `rollup-rpc` endpoint, streamlining the stack for node operators.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage
The week saw active troubleshooting of critical upgrade paths and the identification of potential logic bugs in Superchain synchronization.

### Closed Issues
*   **Dispute Monitor Configuration:** Issue [#20476](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/Retro-Funding/issues/20476) was resolved following technical clarification regarding the interoperability of `op-dispute-mon` with various game types and the role of `op-supernode` in the RPC stack.

### New & Active Issues
*   **op-reth Upgrade Panic:** Discussion persists on [#20462](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/Retro-Funding/issues/20462) regarding a fatal panic (assertion failure in `alloy-trie`) encountered when upgrading `op-reth` from 1.x to 2.x. Testing revealed that the `--engine.legacy-state-root` flag does not resolve the issue, suggesting a non-deterministic bug in parallel trie computation when interacting with legacy database states.
*   **Supernode L1 Verification Logic:** A potential bug was identified in [#20481](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/Retro-Funding/issues/20481) where `op-supernode` may be incorrectly calculating `VerifiedRequiredL1` by using the minimum of per-chain L1s instead of the maximum. Resolution is pending the migration of relevant acceptance tests.
*   **Security Scanning:** A new security tracking issue, [#100](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/Retro-Funding/issues/100), was opened to manage "Wiz" security scans for the main branch.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week centered on deep-dive debugging and architectural alignment. Contributors like `shokeeb-yaqub-vcc` provided detailed technical feedback on the `op-reth` panic, helping to narrow down the cause to trie computation strategies rather than specific blocks. There is also ongoing coordination between maintainers regarding the migration of acceptance tests to validate Supernode logic, as noted by `ajsutton`. The dialogue indicates a high level of technical scrutiny regarding how different components of the Optimism stack (CANNON, KONA, and Supernode) interact.
